tasks.short: Maintain patient recall dates and contact due patients

steps.what: Verify and capture patient recall dates, contact preferences and outstanding appointment status
Maintain due list by filtering verified recall dates and excluding booked patients
Resolve recall exceptions, contact patients and record booking or follow-up outcomes

tasks.design: Configure the due-date view in the existing {OTHER} dental record and recall system. The hygienist captures the clinician's recall decision and contact permissions before a deterministic filter builds the list; the hygienist resolves exceptions and makes patient contact through {TELEPHONY}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual date searches and reconciliation can consume time when recall and booking information are split across views.
tasks.enabler_now: A native due-date filter can use verified fields without interpreting clinical history.
tasks.still_hard: Missing recall instructions, patient choice and failed contacts still need follow-up.
tasks.human_edge: The hygienist checks clinical ambiguity with the responsible clinician and adapts contact to the patient.
tasks.altitude: Own recall completeness and exception follow-up rather than repeatedly compiling lists.

reach.task: Reconcile booking outcomes with recall entries
reach.learn: Use one patient identifier and agreed recall status definitions

evidence.claim: Filtering verified recall dates and excluding existing bookings is a deterministic configuration opportunity; the savings are unmeasured scenario estimates.

assumptions: Boundary covers recall maintenance and contact, not clinical assessment or delivery of treatment.

In s1 the hygienist is the producer of patient ID, clinician-authorized next recall date, instruction provenance, contact permission and preference, booking status and resolution status. All verification and capture time remains in its 30 baseline hours; unclear dates stay unresolved and go to s3, with no inferred interval.

The responsible clinician already produces the clinical recall instruction during care; this design does not add an unpaid clinical review. Any extra clarification is included in s3 and reduces actual savings if larger than assumed.
Use the native recall view first. If it already produces the same list there is no incremental saving; no new interface is assumed.
The system only prepares an internal list; s3 retains all patient contact and recording time.
unknowns: Native recall capabilities and actual manual list-building time
Completeness of dated recall instructions and contact permissions
research_questions: Can the native view reproduce a checked due list including bookings, unresolved dates and patient preferences?
How much time remains in capture and exception handling over a representative recall cycle?

already_counted.description: Resolve exceptions and record patient contact outcomes

incremental.description: Check due-list completeness and maintain filter settings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100, R=30+0+45=75; gross 25%, less 3 hours upkeep gives net 22%. Low 0 if native lists already exist or exception and capture work use the saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Arrange community clinics, confirm group needs and agree dentist referral arrangements
Conduct dental health clinics and adapt explanations and care to participants

tasks.design: Retain clinician-led community clinics, with {CALENDAR} and {DOCS} supporting existing arrangements and {OTHER} holding the clinical record. No new automation is credited because the task mainly involves delivering care, explaining and responding to people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Participant needs, clinical observations and local service arrangements vary at each clinic.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and document tools support the work but establish no new time saving here.
tasks.still_hard: Safe care, consent, understandable explanations and timely dentist referral need professional attention.
tasks.human_edge: The hygienist observes participants and adapts the clinic within authorized clinical practice.
tasks.altitude: Maintain responsibility for accessible, safe community dental services.

reach.task: Agree referral and supervision arrangements for community clinics
reach.learn: Clarify clinical limits and escalation routes before each clinic

evidence.claim: This task-specific assessment retains clinical delivery and coordination; no measured automation saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary includes arranging and conducting the clinic, consent discussions, immediate records and referrals; no separate content-production saving is assumed.
Existing administrative software and clinical records are already available and unchanged.
All collection of participant information and clinical observations remains in s1 and s2. No structured input or automated clinical decision is assumed.
The O*NET statement does not establish a European scope of practice; actual clinical acts depend on local authorization and supervision.
No deployment or new maintenance is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Actual clinic format and authorized procedures
Existing community access and referral arrangements
research_questions: Which part of a real clinic, if any, is repeated administrative preparation rather than direct service?

already_counted.description: Clinic arrangements, consent, care, explanations, records and referrals

incremental.description: No changed process or new software

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100; all clinic work remains. Gross and net saving are zero, with no incremental upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Spend recall effort on complete clinical instructions and patient follow-up while retaining community care.
reach: Coordinate recall outcomes with appointment staff
Agree community referral routes with dentists
role.ambitious_version: A hygienist who maintains a dependable recall process and delivers accessible community dental care.
